papers.title: Anti-correlation time-frequency synergy and dual-granularity fusion for sleep stage classification.
papers.summary: Develops a single-channel EEG sleep staging network using a multi-branch module for anti-correlated frequency features, dual-granularity residual attention fusion, causal transition-aware learning, and focal loss. It reached overall accuracies of 87.0%, 83.4%, and 84.5% on SleepEDF-20, SleepEDF-78, and SHHS, respectively, including N1 accuracies of 57.5%, 52.5%, and 49.3%.

papers.title: Thalamic stereo-EEG detects sleep stages N2 and N3 with discrimination approaching scalp EEG
papers.summary: Analyzed 477 h of simultaneous stereo-EEG and scalp EEG from six adults to test whether thalamic channels identify N2+N3 sleep better than other intracranial sites, using a random forest with HMM decoding and the pretrained SleepSEEG classifier. Thalamic channels performed best among regions sampled in all participants (AUC 0.94 with RF+HMM and 0.93 with SleepSEEG), supporting thalamic N2+N3 detection for sleep-targeted neuromodulation.

papers.title: EEGDash Corpus: A Training-Ready Public Corpus for EEG Foundation Models
papers.summary: Releases eegdash-corpus-v0, a training-ready corpus of 77 public EEG datasets (14,075 hours, 7,272 subjects, 5.0M 10-second samples, 6.21B tokens per epoch) packaged as a chunked Zarr store with per-file SHA-256 and licenses. Retraining REVE-Base from scratch on the corpus yields 0.331 linear-probe and 0.273 fine-tuned scores across seven OpenEEGBench tasks, versus 0.333/0.325 for the released model and 0.200/0.205 for an untrained encoder.

papers.title: Dynamics of Sleep Architecture and Nocturnal Oxygen Saturation During Acclimatization at Intermediate Altitude: A Longitudinal Observational Study in Elite Athletes.
papers.summary: Longitudinally tracked nocturnal sleep architecture and oxygen saturation with wearable EEG and ring oximetry in 17 elite athletes across a 2-week intermediate-altitude training camp (2100 m). Over the first week %N3 decreased and %REM increased logarithmically, with sleep-stage-specific SpO2 recovery and heart-rate dynamics indicating non-uniform acclimatization across sleep stages.

papers.title: Adapting Sleep Foundation Models for Dense Sleep Spindle Localization
papers.summary: Adapts a frozen SleepFM encoder for dense sleep spindle localization by adding a local time-frequency pathway that preserves spindle-relevant spectral content and intra-token position, with residual cross-attention supplying temporal context and localized token-to-sample reconstruction producing dense predictions. On MODA it achieves an event-level F1 of 0.8080 ± 0.0040 at IoU 0.2 across six folds, with ablations showing localization depends mainly on local spectral and sub-token temporal information.

papers.title: A Lightweight EEG-Based Alzheimer's Disease Detection Framework on an Edge-Computing Platform Toward Future Intelligent Digital Twin Systems.
papers.summary: The authors propose a lightweight dilated hybrid deep learning framework with channel selection for EEG-based Alzheimer's disease detection on edge-computing platforms. It achieved 92.56% accuracy on a closed-eye dataset and 75.15% on an open-eye dataset, with inference times of 10.45 ms and 8.23 ms per segment and energy consumption of 9.69 mJ and 6.95 mJ, respectively, demonstrating feasibility for real-time on-edge AD detection.

papers.title: Information leakage and performance overestimation in EEG-based schizophrenia detection: evidence from literature and empirical analyses.
papers.summary: Reviews EEG-based schizophrenia detection literature, finding ~65% of published works use erroneous evaluation practices (epoch-level splitting, pre-partition feature selection) that cause information leakage, and empirically tests this on three open SZ-EEG datasets with leaky versus leakage-free implementations. Information leakage inflated classification accuracy by up to ~30%, prompting calls for best-practice standards before clinical deployment.

papers.title: SafeLens: A Statistically Controlled Nonlinear Machine Learning Framework for Characterizing Hidden Dynamics in Event-Locked Neural Activity
papers.summary: The authors introduce SafeLens, a nonlinear machine learning framework combining random forests with empirical null sampling to statistically control false positives when characterizing event-locked neural activity. In simulated corticocortical evoked potentials injected into intracranial EEG, SafeLens recovered ~2.5 times as many polarity-resolved deflections as trial-average thresholding and the closest data-driven method, with ~5-11 times fewer false components, and in eight patients detected CCEPs above chance until 1,040 ms after stimulation versus 570 and 455 ms for benchmarks.

papers.title: Temporal Associations Between Physiological Sleep and Next-Day Pain Intensity in Individuals With Activity-Limiting Chronic Pain: A Multiple Night At-Home Ear-EEG Sleep-Monitoring Study.
papers.summary: Pre-registered prospective observational study (NCT06368531) using at-home ear-EEG across 11-33 nights in 19 individuals with chronic pain to examine night-to-night sleep variability and its temporal association with next-day pain. Lower next-day pain was associated with greater N3 duration, percentage, and stability, whereas higher pain was linked to N3 fragmentation and higher N1 proportion, with ICC values below 0.5 across many sleep metrics.

papers.title: Synergistic contributions of periodic and aperiodic cortical activity to motor recovery prediction after stroke.
papers.summary: In 41 chronic stroke patients, resting-state EEG was spectrally decomposed into periodic and aperiodic components before and after rehabilitation. Ipsilesional alpha-frequency periodic activity increased with rehabilitation and a model combining higher individual alpha peaks, steeper aperiodic slopes, and their interaction predicted motor recovery (severe group R² = 0.53, balanced accuracy 88%), outperforming a delta-alpha ratio approach.

papers.title: Characterising cortical perturbation-recovery dynamics using TMS-EEG: The Brain Dynamic Toolbox
papers.summary: The study adapted dynamical measures from computational perturbation models to TMS-EEG data and applied them to analyze cortical perturbation-recovery dynamics in 16 healthy adults during long-interval intracortical inhibition (LICI). It found that LICI altered the temporal evolution of dynamical measures: Perturbative Integration Latency Index distinguished conditions in the earliest post-stimulation window, Autocorrelation Function Width differences persisted across a broader early interval, and Lyapunov Exponent showed weaker discrimination, demonstrating that extended post-stimulation trajectories reveal additional features of cortical resilience and temporal memory.

papers.title: Slow power-envelope associations among brain, heart, and gut signals during sleep: an exploratory multivariate transfer entropy study.
papers.summary: Using overnight EEG, ECG, and bowel sound recordings from 24 healthy subjects, the study applied multivariate transfer entropy to quantify directed slow power-envelope associations among brain, heart, and gut across sleep stages. Information flow from heart to brain, brain to gut, and heart to gut consistently exceeded reverse directions, with sleep-stage-dependent dissociation of within- versus inter-system flow, presented as exploratory statistical patterns.

papers.title: Dissociable Oscillatory Alpha and Aperiodic Neural Dynamics Underlie Atypical Attentional Control in Children With Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD)
papers.summary: EEG from 45 children with ADHD and 45 typically developing children during a visual detection task was parameterized into oscillatory alpha and aperiodic components. Demand-related attentional differences appeared only in oscillatory alpha, whereas distractor-related abnormalities were reflected in the aperiodic slope, and multivariate machine learning classification based on these signatures robustly discriminated ADHD from controls.

papers.title: Augmented reality paradigm and EA-DGCNN decoding algorithm for motor imagery in stroke patients.
papers.summary: Proposes a wearable augmented reality motor-imagery BCI training paradigm and a Euclidean Alignment-based Dynamic Graph CNN (EA-DGCNN) decoding architecture with attention, dynamic graph attention, multi-scale convolutions, and a Broad Learning System. The model reaches 85.13 ± 10.53% on BCI Competition IV 2a and 83.67 ± 8.52% cross-subject on PhysioNet, while the AR paradigm achieves 71.9 ± 8.9% versus 68.9 ± 8.0% for 2D training in 20 stroke patients.

papers.title: False-Positive Calls of Reimplemented Published Analyses for Covert Command-Following on Electroencephalograms Recorded Without Study Commands
papers.summary: Reimplemented 11 published EEG analyses for covert command-following on recordings made without commands and found that three (Goldfine 2011, du Bois 2026, Guger 2018) falsely called significantly more than 5% positive, up to 27.3% after cardiac arrest, while still detecting genuine responses. The authors argue that any positive call rule must report its false-call rate and detection at that rate.

papers.title: Age-specific pediatric templates improve EEG source-reconstructed biomarkers in children
papers.summary: Compared EEG source-reconstructed biomarkers using individual MRI, age-specific pediatric templates (ages 6-17), and the adult fsaverage template in 384 children aged 5.5-17.5 years. Pediatric templates matched individual MRI-based biomarker values more closely than the adult template across power, DFA, and fE/I measures up to about age 12, supporting their use when individual MRI is unavailable.

papers.title: Decoding sequence auditory expectations for clinical diagnostic and prognostic assessment of prolonged disorders of consciousness.
papers.summary: Developed a low-demand modified local-global auditory paradigm with single-trial machine-learning frameworks (CCA, PCA, xDAWN) to decode expectations of global regularity, improving single-trial classification of global effects by up to 15% versus the original paradigm. In 20 prolonged DOC patients, derived awareness criteria reached 68.8% diagnostic and 60.5% prognostic balanced accuracy.

papers.title: Feedback Valence, Prediction Error, and the Limits of Computational Attribution in Symptom-Related EEG
papers.summary: Re-analyzed an anxiety-related feedback-locked EEG association across two open probabilistic-learning datasets, finding greater trait anxiety linked to larger negative-minus-positive FCz theta responses but no established theta specificity. Feedback valence and signed prediction error were nearly collinear (r=-0.964), and signed PE added only limited held-out predictive value beyond valence, constraining computational attribution at the individual level.

papers.title: Affective burden and resting-state EEG microstate dynamics in sleep-severity-matched chronic insomnia.
papers.summary: Matched 21 pairs of treatment-naive chronic insomnia patients on sleep severity to compare resting-state EEG microstates between low and high affective burden. High affective burden showed greater microstate C coverage and lower microstate D coverage/occurrence/duration during eyes-open rest, with a cross-validated classification AUC of 74.8%.

papers.title: Transforming neurophysiological data into measurable stress metric using machine learning-based stress quantification framework for smart factory workers.
papers.summary: Proposed and tested an integrated framework combining EEG, fNIRS, gaze tracking, and machine learning for continuous mental stress estimation in smart factory workers. Ensemble models using STAI scores as target achieved 84.1% classification accuracy and RMSE 10.86 for regression, with behavioral and subjective measures reflecting process-variable effects.

papers.title: PINR-ESI: Physics-Informed Self-Supervised Implicit Neural Representation Framework for EEG Extended-Source Imaging
papers.summary: Proposes a physics-informed self-supervised implicit neural representation (INR) framework for EEG extended-source imaging that uses the lead field matrix and forward-model agreement instead of paired synthetic supervised labels. Simulations showed the clearest advantage for identifying active cortical regions with multiple and larger sources, and real epilepsy and intracranial stimulation EEG evaluations supported feasibility.

papers.title: EEG emotion-recognition datasets for neuroarchitecture: an appraisal of openness, AI-readiness and ontology maturity.
papers.summary: Following PRISMA 2020, this systematic review appraised 27 publicly obtainable EEG emotion-recognition datasets using a 52-criterion codebook across openness (FAIR), AI-readiness, and ontology maturity; none were designed for spatial neuroarchitecture research. Openness was weakest for Interoperability (2.044 vs FAIR composite 2.857), only 8 datasets were fully open, and ontology levels clustered at Level 3 with none at Levels 4-5.

papers.title: Generative-augmented multimodal neuroaffective decoding for product evaluation: toward neurofeedback-driven human-in-the-loop co-design.
papers.summary: Introduces GAMAF, a generative-augmented multimodal fusion model combining cWGAN-GP, cross-modal attention, graph-based interactions, and adaptive weighting to decode perceived attractiveness, innovativeness, and friendliness from EEG, eye tracking, and peripheral signals in 150 participant-stimulus trials. GAMAF reached mean outer-fold R² of 0.810, 0.850, and 0.840, exceeding a Multimodal Transformer baseline and reducing aggregate MAE and RMSE by about 29.6% and 29.7%.

papers.title: Elevated neuronal excitability and seizure susceptibility in a mouse model of SCN2A-related developmental and epileptic encephalopathy.
papers.summary: Generated and characterized a novel Scn2a-E430A mouse model of SCN2A-related developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, finding hippocampal pyramidal neuron hyperexcitability, enhanced CA1 long-term potentiation, recurrent epileptiform discharges, and faster seizure generalization with greater lethality despite normal seizure initiation. Phenytoin pretreatment improved seizure outcomes across induction methods.

papers.title: An Eyewear-Based EEG Interface for Temporal-Region Monitoring and Emotion Recognition
papers.summary: The authors developed an eyewear-based EEG system with dry titanium electrodes near T7/T8 and evaluated it across 103 recordings in five paradigms, retaining 93.2-100.0% of epochs after quality control. Emotion decoding yielded balanced accuracies of 0.882 (two-class) and 0.667 (three-class), and the system outperformed the Muse headband in group-held-out classification.

papers.title: Multiscale Neurodynamic Alterations in Major Depressive Disorder Revealed by Lempel-Ziv Complexity of Multi-Paradigm Resting-State EEG.
papers.summary: Using multiscale Lempel-Ziv complexity, the authors compared resting-state EEG multiscale dynamics between patients with major depressive disorder and healthy controls, deriving Scale-Dependent Variation Slope and Cross-Scale Correlation Coefficient features. Patients showed impaired complexity transitions from low to high frequencies and disrupted delta-centered cross-scale integration, with classification reaching a maximum accuracy of 85.71%.

papers.title: EEG-based listened-language classification
papers.summary: Recorded EEG from subjects listening to sentences in five languages and used channel-energy features with bi-LSTM, LSTM, and GRU networks to classify language and comprehension level. Accuracy was 36.37% for five-language classification, 81.36% for understood/partially understood/not understood, and 89.09% for native versus foreign language, with bi-LSTM performing best overall.

papers.title: Integrating uncertainty and practice variability for epilepsy prognostication after intracranial EEG: A meta-analysis.
papers.summary: Meta-analysis of 115 studies of epilepsy surgery after intracranial EEG found that 67% of patients proceeded to resection, 52% achieved seizure freedom, and 58% had a favorable outcome; individual patient-level models identified lesional MRI and cortical malformation as predictors of favorable outcome and bilateral implantation as predictive of less favorable outcome. The models were well calibrated but showed only modest discrimination.

papers.title: Nociceptive-evoked electroencephalography can predict inter-individual differences in high frequency induced sensitisation of central nociceptive pathways: A test-retest reliability study
papers.summary: Applied high-frequency stimulation (HFS) across two identical sessions to assess test-retest reliability of pinprick- and electrically evoked EEG features and their relation to individual differences in hyperalgesia development. Reliability was poor-to-moderate and worsened for post-HFS change measures, though contralateral alpha-ERD was strengthened post-HFS and baseline alpha-ERD related to the subsequent time course of secondary hyperalgesia, while vertex potential magnitude tracked general pain intensity.

papers.title: Cannabidiol and fronto-parietal EEG connectivity in autistic children.
papers.summary: In a double-blind placebo-controlled crossover trial, 12 weeks of oral cannabidiol increased beta-band resting-state EEG functional connectivity between right frontal and right inferior-parietal electrodes (F4-P8) in autistic children, with no comparable change after placebo. The authors report this as preliminary evidence requiring replication in larger samples.

papers.title: Cortical evoked potentials from deep brain stimulation of the superolateral medial forebrain bundle: An exploratory study.
papers.journal: Clinical neurophysiology : official journal of the International Federation of Clinical Neurophysiology
papers.summary: In 7 patients receiving deep brain stimulation of the superolateral medial forebrain bundle, cortical evoked potentials were recorded using epidural ECoG (n=4) or high-density EEG (n=3), with responses observed in 5 of 7 patients and consistent latencies and prefrontal topographies; oculomotor co-activation was present in 6 of 7 but differed in timing and morphology. This first exploratory study demonstrates electrophysiological connectivity between the slMFB-DBS target and prefrontal cortex in humans.

papers.title: Advancing Repetitive Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation for Depression: Novel Protocols, Precision Targeting, and Future Directions.
papers.summary: This expert opinion reviews recent advances in repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) for depression, covering novel protocols such as theta-burst stimulation, accelerated and priming regimens, MRI-guided targeting, and closed-loop systems using real-time EEG or fNIRS feedback. It discusses challenges including cost, standardization, and technical barriers, and outlines future directions for improving rTMS efficiency, precision, and accessibility.

papers.title: A high robustness decoding technique for ultrasound modulated electroencephalogram.
papers.summary: Developed a robust decoding algorithm for ultrasound-modulated EEG based on ultrasound pulse repetition frequency and introduced the acoustoelectric modulation ratio (AMR) to classify coupling conditions. Across simulations, phantoms, and human SSVEP data from 10 volunteers, the algorithm achieved 0.79 mm encoding spatial resolution and outperformed four traditional methods under weak, moderate, and over-modulation conditions (average decoding correlations 0.84-0.90).

papers.title: Yield of epileptiform abnormalities and predictors on routine electroencephalography in a neurology facility in Ghana.
papers.summary: In a retrospective analysis of 124 patients who underwent routine outpatient EEG at a Ghanaian tertiary center, epileptiform discharges were found in 72 patients (58.1% yield), with generalized epilepsy accounting for 83.3% of abnormalities. Abnormal EEG background activity was the only independent predictor of epileptiform discharges (aOR = 23.47, 95% CI: 2.95–186.86, p = 0.003).

papers.title: Resting-State EEG Graph Analysis Reveals Enhanced Alpha-Band Integration in High-IQ Individuals: The MENSA-Connect Project.
papers.summary: Compared resting-state 64-channel EEG functional connectivity (lagged linear coherence) between 29 MENSA high-IQ participants and 20 controls using sLORETA-based graph theory. High-IQ individuals showed shorter alpha-band characteristic path length (greater global integration) and higher beta-band clustering coefficient with longer path length (greater local specialization), with no group differences in small-worldness across bands.

papers.title: Impairment of ictal consciousness and psychosis in drug-resistant focal epilepsy: A retrospective clinical cohort study.
papers.summary: In a retrospective cohort of 232 seizures from adults with drug-resistant focal epilepsy, the probability of psychosis of epilepsy peaked at intermediate scores on the Consciousness Seizure Scale (GEE, OR = 4.31, p = .006), independent of epilepsy and seizure duration. The findings suggest that partial disruption of ictal awareness may favor the emergence of psychotic symptoms.

papers.title: Profound EEG Suppression Does Not Justify Discontinuation of Anesthesia and Analgesia.
papers.summary: Argues that profound EEG suppression during anesthesia does not justify discontinuing anesthesia and analgesia, addressing the interpretation of burst-suppression and suppressed EEG as a signal for reducing anesthetic delivery.

papers.title: Matching Corticospinal and Cortical Excitability along the motor cortex: TMS-EMG-EEG study
papers.summary: Combined TMS with EMG and EEG in 24 subjects to relate cortical excitability thresholds (CETs, EEG) to resting motor thresholds (RMTs, EMG) at hand, arm, and leg hotspots along M1. RMTs and CETs were strongly correlated and both increased from hand to arm to leg, CETs were generally lower than RMTs, and within-subject CET-RMT differences occurred at all sites, increasing from hand to leg.

papers.title: Microgravity and Cardiac Electrophysiology: Autonomic Remodeling, Arrhythmogenesis, and Implications for Long-Duration Spaceflight.
papers.summary: This review describes cardiac electrophysiological alterations in microgravity, including autonomic resetting, spatiotemporal heterogeneity, and QTc prolongation that create an arrhythmogenic substrate, with documented transient premature atrial and ventricular complexes and possible early-onset atrial fibrillation. It also discusses NASA's countermeasures (exercise, electrolyte monitoring, wearable telemetry, automated CPR) and risks for long-duration deep-space missions.

papers.title: Dual-modal synaptic operation in a van der Waals heterostructure for emotion-inspired neuromorphic processing.
papers.summary: Fabricated bimodally modulated artificial synapses from a van der Waals-stacked GQD/MoS2 heterostructure that integrate dopamine (1-5 nM) and optical stimuli, showing synergistic postsynaptic current enhancement and stable plasticity over 1000 s. Device-informed simulations reached 73.4% accuracy on facial emotion recognition (FER-2013, CNN) and 76.6% on EEG-inspired PSC temporal-signal classification (SVM).

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
